title: [CQ-V04b1] Runner channel client
description:
Objective: give the host's trusted check runner (CQ-V04b) a client for the daemon's authenticated /runner channel, through which it calls moe.* tools. It is the only local-runner code that ever reads the runner key.

Split from CQ-V04b (task-340a07b33a764c65b2486d16b30d7aef) on 2026-10-29 for size (QA's 400-net cap). It builds on CQ-V03a (task-3b4e3833, landed in 1607abf):
- server/runnerChannel.ts: RUNNER_KEY_HEADER is 'x-moe-runner-key', and runnerKeyPath(projectPath) gives <MOE_RUNNER_KEY_DIR | ~/.moe/runner-keys>/<first 32 hex of sha256(projectPath)>.key.
- WebSocketServer serves `/runner` and accepts loopback only; an authentication failure closes with 1008.
- McpAdapter answers JSON-RPC tools/call. A result is {result: {content: [{type: 'text', text: <JSON>}]}}; an error is {error: {code, message, data: {tool, codeName}}}.

Contract: a new scripts/local-runner/runner-client.mjs, Node stdlib only.
- openRunnerChannel({ projectPath, timeoutMs, signal }) resolves { call(tool, args, { signal }), close() }, or rejects with exactly one fixed RUNNER_* code.
- Discovery: read <projectPath>/.moe/daemon.json under a size cap. It must name the same projectPath, a loopback bindHost (absent, 127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost) and an integer port; otherwise RUNNER_DAEMON_INFO_INVALID. Reuse guest-session.mjs's daemon.json rules if they can be exported unchanged; otherwise mirror them.
- Key: the file at runnerKeyPath's location for the daemon.json projectPath. It must hold exactly 43 base64url characters, allowing one trailing newline; otherwise RUNNER_KEY_INVALID. A missing file is RUNNER_KEY_MISSING.
- Transport: globalThis.WebSocket (Node 22+; verified on Node 24 to send custom headers via `new WebSocket(url, { headers })`), connecting to ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/runner with the key header.
  - A missing WebSocket is RUNNER_WEBSOCKET_UNAVAILABLE.
  - A 1008 close is RUNNER_AUTH_REFUSED.
- call sends `tools/call {name, arguments}` with a unique id and resolves the parsed tool result.
  - A tool error rejects with RUNNER_TOOL_ERROR, carrying the daemon's numeric code and codeName.
  - A per-call timeout is RUNNER_CALL_TIMEOUT.
  - A disconnect rejects every pending call with RUNNER_DISCONNECTED.
  - close() is idempotent.
- The key value never appears in any error message or property, return value or log line.

Out of scope: dispatch logic (CQ-V04b), any daemon change, and enabling verified-local.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-channel.test.mjs (on WSL: env -i with the nvm Node 24 PATH). Add the file to the CI local-runner step's explicit list in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
definitionOfDone: openRunnerChannel reaches the loopback /runner endpoint named by the project's daemon.json, sending x-moe-runner-key from the file at runnerKeyPath's location. A missing or invalid daemon.json, key file or WebSocket, or a 1008 close, refuses with its fixed RUNNER_* code.

Against the real daemon /runner endpoint, call() resolves a tool's parsed result, rejects a tool error with RUNNER_TOOL_ERROR carrying the daemon's codeName, and rejects every pending call on timeout or disconnect.
A sentinel key value never appears in any error, return value, log line or test output.
Fresh verification `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-channel.test.mjs` exits 0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (red). Load test-driven-development.

Create scripts/tests/local-runner-channel.test.mjs (node:test). Keep it to about 200 lines, because tests count toward QA's 400-net cap. Assert exact `code` values (plus rpcCode and codeName where set), never truthiness.

CORRECTIONS to the task description, so the client matches the daemon:
- The key file must hold EXACTLY 43 base64url characters with NO trailing newline: server/runnerChannel.ts KEY_RE /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/ is applied to the raw file, so the daemon itself refuses a newline.
- A loopback bindHost is absent, '127.0.0.1' or '::1' only, as in guest-session.mjs: no 'localhost', and no DNS.

Cases without a daemon, using temp dirs and an injectable `WebSocket` option:
- C1, daemon.json. Each of these gives RUNNER_DAEMON_INFO_INVALID: missing, a directory, more than MAX_DAEMON_INFO_BYTES (import it from scripts/local-runner/guest-session.mjs), not JSON, not a record, projectPath unequal to path.resolve(input), port not an integer in 1-65535. bindHost '0.0.0.0' and 'localhost' each give RUNNER_DAEMON_NOT_LOOPBACK.
- C2, key. A missing file is RUNNER_KEY_MISSING. 42 characters, 44 characters, a trailing newline, a non-base64url character, or a directory is RUNNER_KEY_INVALID. The key's location honours MOE_RUNNER_KEY_DIR (trimmed and resolved), else <home>/.moe/runner-keys, with <first 32 hex of sha256(daemon.json projectPath)>.key. The file name is pinned against a fixed vector.
- C3: `WebSocket: undefined` is RUNNER_WEBSOCKET_UNAVAILABLE, with no read of the key.

Cases against the REAL daemon (DoD 2):
- Start it as scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs does: packages/moe-daemon/dist/index.js `init --project <tmp> --port <free>`. Use an env with every MOE_* removed, HOME and USERPROFILE set to a temp profile, MOE_RUNNER_KEY_DIR set to a temp dir, and LOG_LEVEL warn. Wait for .moe/daemon.json with a bounded poll, and stop the daemon in after(). If dist is missing, FAIL with 'build packages/moe-daemon first'; never skip.
- C4 success: call('moe.list_tasks', {}) resolves the parsed tool result object.
- C5 tool error: call('moe.get_context', {taskId: 'task-0000000000000000000000000000dead'}) rejects RUNNER_TOOL_ERROR with the daemon's exact rpcCode and codeName (assert the observed values).
- C6 auth: a different valid key in another MOE_RUNNER_KEY_DIR makes openRunnerChannel reject RUNNER_AUTH_REFUSED (close 1008).
- C7 timeout: a long-poll the daemon parks (moe.wait_for_task, or another tool marked blocking) with call timeoutMs 500 rejects RUNNER_CALL_TIMEOUT. The channel stays usable: a following list_tasks resolves.
- C8 disconnect: two pending calls, then the daemon is stopped. Both reject RUNNER_DISCONNECTED, a later call rejects RUNNER_DISCONNECTED, and close() twice is harmless.

C9 sentinel (DoD 3): across C1 to C8, write a known sentinel key wherever a key file exists. Then:
- String(err), JSON.stringify(err, Object.getOwnPropertyNames(err)) and every resolved value never contain it;
- console.log, console.warn and console.error spies record nothing from the module;
- the test's own assertion messages never interpolate the key.

Run `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-channel.test.mjs`: every case fails.

Create scripts/local-runner/runner-client.mjs. Node stdlib only, about 130 lines, and no logger or console use at all. The header comment states:
- it is the only local-runner code that reads the runner key;
- it reaches only the loopback daemon named by daemon.json;
- error messages carry fixed codes only, never a path, key byte or upstream text, in guest-session.mjs's style.

Error handling: every failure rejects with exactly one fixed RUNNER_* code, via Object.assign(new Error('Runner channel failed: <code>.'), { code }), plus rpcCode and codeName for tool errors. Each pending call settles exactly once, and nothing throws synchronously out of an event handler.

Exports:
- `RUNNER_KEY_HEADER = 'x-moe-runner-key'`, mirroring server/runnerChannel.ts.
- `runnerKeyFile(projectPath, env = process.env)`, the exact mirror of runnerKeyPath.
- `openRunnerChannel({ projectPath, timeoutMs = 30_000, signal, WebSocket = globalThis.WebSocket })`.

openRunnerChannel, in order:
1. Validate the inputs; failure is RUNNER_INPUT_INVALID.
2. If typeof WebSocket !== 'function': RUNNER_WEBSOCKET_UNAVAILABLE.
3. Read daemon.json under guest-session's discipline: O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK, isFile, the size cap and a record. Then require projectPath === path.resolve(input), an integer port, and bindHost absent or in {'127.0.0.1', '::1'}.
4. Read the key through the same open discipline, with a size of at most 64 bytes and KEY_RE exact. ENOENT is RUNNER_KEY_MISSING; anything else is RUNNER_KEY_INVALID.
5. Open `new WebSocket(\`ws://${host}:${port}/runner\`, { headers: { [RUNNER_KEY_HEADER]: key } })`, where host is the bindHost or 127.0.0.1, bracketed for ::1.
   - Resolve on 'open'.
   - A 'close' with code 1008 before open is RUNNER_AUTH_REFUSED. Any other failure before open is RUNNER_CONNECT_FAILED.
   - No open within timeoutMs is RUNNER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT. A signal abort is RUNNER_ABORTED.
   - Drop the key reference after construction.

call(tool, args, { signal, timeoutMs }):
- Requires tool /^moe\.[a-z_]+$/ and a plain-object args; otherwise RUNNER_CALL_INVALID.
- Sends {jsonrpc: '2.0', id: <increasing int>, method: 'tools/call', params: {name, arguments}}.
- result.content[0].text parsed as JSON resolves; a malformed result is RUNNER_RESPONSE_INVALID.
- error rejects RUNNER_TOOL_ERROR with rpcCode (number) and codeName (string, when present).
- A timeout (RUNNER_CALL_TIMEOUT) or an abort (RUNNER_ABORTED) drops the pending entry, and a late response is ignored.
- Unmatched or garbage messages are ignored.

After open, a 'close' or 'error' rejects every pending call, and every later call, with RUNNER_DISCONNECTED. close() is idempotent and rejects pending calls the same way.

Make every case pass.

.github/workflows/ci.yml: append scripts/tests/local-runner-channel.test.mjs to the explicit file list of the 'Test local runner prerequisite bundles' step (`node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs … local-runner-check.test.mjs`). Nothing else changes. That step runs after 'Build daemon' in the build-all-platforms job on all three OSes, so the real-daemon cases have dist. Confirm this against the file before editing, and report it in the step note.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
scripts/local-runner/runner-client.mjs opens the daemon's authenticated /runner channel and calls moe.* tools over it.
- It discovers the daemon only through <project>/.moe/daemon.json: the same projectPath, an integer port, and a bindHost that is absent, 127.0.0.1 or ::1.
- It reads the key only from the file server/runnerChannel.ts runnerKeyPath names: MOE_RUNNER_KEY_DIR or ~/.moe/runner-keys, then <32 hex of sha256(daemon projectPath)>.key, exactly 43 base64url characters.
- It connects with Node's built-in WebSocket and the x-moe-runner-key header.
- call() returns the parsed tool result, or rejects with a fixed RUNNER_* code; tool errors carry the daemon's rpcCode and codeName. Timeouts, aborts and disconnects reject the affected pending calls.
- No message ever carries the key, a path or upstream text, and the module never logs.
acceptanceCriteria: Every discovery, key and transport refusal has its own fixed code, and none of them writes to the network.

Against the real daemon: a tool result resolves, a tool error rejects RUNNER_TOOL_ERROR with the daemon's codeName, a wrong key is RUNNER_AUTH_REFUSED, a parked call times out with RUNNER_CALL_TIMEOUT while the channel stays usable, and stopping the daemon rejects every pending call with RUNNER_DISCONNECTED.
A sentinel key never appears in any error, value or console output.
invariants: Only loopback hosts are dialled, and only the daemon.json of the given project is trusted.
The key is read once per open and never stored, returned, logged or put in messages.
Each pending call settles exactly once.
No daemon change, no Git writes, no .moe edits.
compatibility: It mirrors server/runnerChannel.ts (RUNNER_KEY_HEADER, runnerKeyPath, KEY_RE) and guest-session.mjs's daemon.json discipline exactly; it changes neither.
Node 22+ (global WebSocket). An older Node refuses with RUNNER_WEBSOCKET_UNAVAILABLE.
approvedScope: New scripts/local-runner/runner-client.mjs: RUNNER_KEY_HEADER, runnerKeyFile and openRunnerChannel.
reuse: MAX_DAEMON_INFO_BYTES is imported from scripts/local-runner/guest-session.mjs, and its open/size/record discipline is mirrored, because daemonRefusal is private and returns only a code.
scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs's real-daemon start: an env without MOE_*, a temp HOME, `init --project --port`, a daemon.json poll, and stop.
Node's global WebSocket, so there is no new dependency.
sourceAssumptions: packages/moe-daemon/src/server/runnerChannel.ts: RUNNER_KEY_HEADER is 'x-moe-runner-key'. runnerKeyPath(projectPath) uses MOE_RUNNER_KEY_DIR (trimmed, path.resolve) or os.homedir()/.moe/runner-keys, plus sha256(projectPath) hex[:32] + '.key'. authenticateRunner applies KEY_RE /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/ to the raw stored file and accepts loopback only.
packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts: an exact '/runner' pathname; an authentication failure closes 1008 'runner authentication failed'; then the same attachMcpClient as /mcp.
packages/moe-daemon/src/server/McpAdapter.ts: a tools/call result is {content: [{type: 'text', text: JSON}]}. A MoeError becomes {error: {code, message, data: {tool, codeName}}}.
packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts writes daemon.json {port, pid, startedAt, projectPath, bindHost only when not the default} after listening, and calls ensureRunnerKey(projectPath) at startup.
Verified in this session: Node v24.21.0's global WebSocket sends custom headers via `new WebSocket(url, { headers })`.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Transport: Node's global WebSocket, CHOSEN; verified here to send custom headers. Rejected: the ws package, which scripts/local-runner has no dependency on; a hand-rolled RFC 6455 client, more code and more risk; reusing moe-proxy, which speaks /mcp and has no key.
2. daemon.json rules: exporting guest-session.mjs's daemonRefusal would change an R-series file, and it returns only a code. Instead, mirror its discipline and import the exported MAX_DAEMON_INFO_BYTES.
3. Tests: a real daemon for the DoD 2 cases, which proves the actual /runner auth and JSON-RPC shapes; onboarding.mjs is the precedent. Injected fakes only for the no-daemon refusals.
4. Error text carries fixed codes only, no upstream message, matching guest-session's sessionError discipline. The daemon's codeName and rpcCode are kept as properties.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- The task description allowed one trailing newline in the key, but the daemon's KEY_RE does not, so the plan requires exactly 43 characters.
- The description allowed 'localhost', but guest-session's LOOPBACK set is {127.0.0.1, ::1} only. The plan follows the code.
- runnerKeyPath hashes the daemon's projectPath string, so the client must hash daemon.json's projectPath, not the caller's spelling.
- The CI local-runner step is in build-all-platforms, after Build daemon. Verify this before relying on dist.
- onboarding.mjs isolates env: no MOE_*, HOME and USERPROFILE set to a temp profile, NODE_ENV production, LOG_LEVEL warn.
planningNotes.risks:
- The real daemon in tests: free-port races, slow starts on Windows CI, and stopping it on every path, including failures. Bound every wait and stop the daemon in after().
- A timeout case needs a tool the daemon parks (blocking: true). Pick one that does not register a worker, or clean it up.
- A WSL client cannot read a Windows daemon's key (a different HOME): unsupported, refused with RUNNER_KEY_MISSING.
- Windows: O_NOFOLLOW is 0, so the symlink guard is POSIX-only, as in guest-session.
- No daemon change at all. A daemon defect found here becomes a separate bug task.
